transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been having a hard time since I moved into this busted-up room. I’m up late trying to fix leaks and deal with the heat, then I’m dragging into work late and messing up things I normally handle. And I’ve been snapping at people more than I should.
How long ago did you move into this new place, and how long have you been experiencing these sleep problems, lateness, and irritability?
About a month now. It started shortly after I moved into that room in Bridgeport.
Besides feeling irritable and stressed, have you noticed yourself feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?
No, I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down all the time or anything. It’s mostly just stress and being on edge.
Have you been feeling nervous, worried, or on edge most of the time since this started, beyond just being irritable?
Yeah, I’ve been pretty on edge. I keep worrying about getting the room fixed and then I’m up dealing with it, so by the time I get to work I’m dragging and messing things up. It’s been getting to me.
Would you say that the worry and feeling on edge is the main thing bothering you day-to-day, more than any other emotional symptom?
Yeah, I think so. I’m stressed about that room all the time—fixing the leaks, the heat—and it’s got me on edge. Then I’m not sleeping, I’m late to work, and I’ve been snapping at people.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms of anxiety, irritability, and sleep disturbance emerged within one month of a clearly identifiable psychosocial stressor (moving into a dilapidated apartment with ongoing repair issues). The predominant symptom is anxiety/worry rather than depressed mood, and there is no evidence of a full depressive episode, generalized anxiety disorder predating the stressor, or trauma exposure meeting PTSD criteria. Functional impairment (lateness, work errors, interpersonal friction) is present but proportionate to the stressor and time-limited, consistent with Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety.
